title: Ginger Spice Brownies
changes_from_base: Fresh and ground ginger with warm spices whipped into the eggs; crystallised ginger on top.
summary: Fudgy brownies whipped with fresh and ground ginger, coriander, allspice, nutmeg, cardamom and clove.
equipment: 20 cm square metal baking tin, lined with baking paper
heatproof bowl and small pan (or a microwave)
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: dark muscovado or dark brown soft sugar
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan) and line the tin.

steps.title: Melt
steps.text: Warm the butter in a small pan until it just simmers, take it off the heat and stir in the chopped chocolate; it will look thin.

steps.title: Whip
steps.text: Whisk the sugars, cold eggs, vanilla, fresh and ground ginger, salt and the other spices on high speed for about 5 min, until pale, thick and doubled.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: On low speed pour in the warm chocolate butter, then sift over the flour and cocoa and fold until no streaks remain.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Spread in the tin, scatter the crystallised ginger over and bake about 30 min, until puffed and a cocktail stick comes out with a few moist crumbs.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool completely in the tin, then lift out and cut into 16 squares.

tips: Whipping the eggs well gives a glossy, crackly top.
Grate the fresh ginger on a fine grater so it melts into the batter.
Cold eggs whip up thicker and more stable.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 2 months.
